findings.evidence: [F2] asserts that every regular common level is an embedded n-dimensional Lagrangian fibre and that the fields X_{F_i} are tangent, independent, and span its tangent space. It cites only the definition of Lagrangian submanifolds, which does not establish these regular-level facts. Steps 1.1 and 8.1 use them. Derive them from the submersion normal form, involution, and nondegeneracy, or cite the exact regular-level theorem with its hypotheses. Cannas da Silva states the matching regular-level fact immediately before Theorem 18.12, Lecture 18, pp. 109–111: [source](https://www.math.ist.utl.pt/~acannas/Books/symplectic.pdf).

The proof uses d(σ*ω)=σ*(dω), d(π*α)=π*(dα), and the analogous identity for β_i, but [F5] cites Cartan's formula and flow differentiation, not pullback naturality. The exact published statement is d(F*η)=F*(dη) in thm-the-exterior-derivative-commutes-with-pullback; it lies only indirectly in this item's dependency closure and is not identified at these uses. Name/apply that supplier or prove the required coordinate identities locally.

The proof asserts that every smooth function constant on the fibres factors as G∘π for a smooth G on B_0, without deriving or citing smooth descent. Use the local projection charts supplied by cor-local-normal-form-for-submersions to construct local factors and show they agree on overlaps.

def-action-and-angle-coordinates gives θ_i values in R/Z. The formula 2πθ_i has no declared target quotient, and multiplication by 2π is not a map on R/Z with that same codomain. Specify the map [x]↦[2πx] into R/(2πZ) and the corresponding smooth quotient charts.

The statement allows arbitrary n and h on an n-dimensional action domain, but the chain-rule line ∂_i\tilde h=2π h'(2πI_i^rad) gives h a scalar argument and does not select its ith partial derivative. The correct coordinate formula is ∂_i\tilde h(I^rad)=2π(∂_i h)(2πI^rad). The Hamilton-equation claim is derived before this invalid consistency calculation.

The Statement proves measure preservation only for bounded Borel A with closure contained in the fixed-time flow domain. The final remark claims the same for arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable A by exhausting with bounded Borel sets; a non-Borel Lebesgue-measurable set is not such a union, and no null-set-preservation argument is supplied. Either prove the extension using local C1 null-set preservation/change of variables or keep the title and remark within the stated class.

findings.location: Statement, opening paragraph defining C and the descended forms
findings.evidence: The cited torus and quotient-topology definitions specify a topological quotient, but the statement uses smooth forms, a C∞ diffeomorphism, and pullbacks on C=(R/Z)×R without specifying a smooth atlas or establishing that π:R²→C is a local diffeomorphism. Define the quotient smooth structure and justify the descent of the invariant forms before using these operations.

The published definition calls B×(R/Z)^n the target of a diffeomorphism but does not specify its smooth quotient structure; its only dependency is the symplectic-manifold definition. The local torus supplier defines quotient topology, not smooth charts. The cited Meinrenken Definitions 6.16 and 6.18, pp. 72–74, use the smooth quotient T*B/Λ, but the definition does not state or transfer that structure: [source](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/mein/teaching/LectureNotes/symplectic.pdf). Define the standard quotient smooth structure and its charts.

The proof uses dist(z,K) to define a compact tube H, then asserts distance attainment and that H is closed and bounded. No dependency defines point-to-set distance or these tube properties. Define dist(z,K)=inf_{k∈K}||z-k||_2 and prove the needed Lipschitz/compact-neighbourhood properties, or cite an exact supplier.

The proof sets L=sup_H||DF|| and uses this operator norm in hL≤1/2, but neither def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient nor the other dependencies define the operator norm on DF(x):R^n→R^n. Add the exact finite-dimensional operator-norm definition and Euclidean norm convention.
